answer: Make each agent prove it stores its own uniquely sealed copy of a shared archive. At random moments the network sends a whisper of a challenge, a few random byte offsets, and the agent must answer within two seconds from its own replica. Each copy is encoded with an identity-specific pigment, so clones cannot share one relic of data on a single disk. A 100 GB replica costs about $2 a month, so 1,000 fake agents cost an attacker roughly $2,000 every month.
